What importance do we put on an FTR that isn't a FL? The FTR to the FL has caught my attention so far. I from what I have seen a reaction should be expected there and it should be trade able as long as you look at the bigger picture.

People like to trade the same things in different ways. Dissecting IF's trades really helped me learn a lot, I hope I'm learning the correct things. IF seems to just go straight for the source as long as he has confirmation PA, and he then exits at the source of a move when he has confirmation that source will be the turning point for a move in the opposite direction. I think this is just part of IF's trading plan. Others look at the same area but take the trade after more confirmation.

That brings me nicely on to creating my own trading plan, how can I possibly think about becoming a trading without a plan.

1. Money management, the key. What am I willing to risk per trade? 2. What am I going to trade? Just FL's? FTR's? Only certain FTR's. Will I take multiple trades on the what I consider to be one move if I get additional confirmation PA that allows for another entry? 3. How many trades will I have open at any one time? 4. How many pairs/commodities will I monitor? I can't monitor them all, which ones will I chose? etc

What I've been looking for are basic rules, rules to follow the market, rules to put on top of my foundation of money management. If I have an engulf, I look for an entry. Looking at the charts this morning I'm realized I need more time in front of the charts to train myself and make this second nature, or close to.

I really believe price will go back to the source of a move if an engulf occurs, it's keeping an eye on what else has been engulfed.

Anyway, I've rambled far too much, I just had a lot of thoughts I needed to get out of my head. Hopefully at least one person can learn from my struggles, and if I might be heading in the wrong direction please just let me know.

In IF's chart I believe the first blue box is the FLAG, the red box isn't the FL of this FLAG, this is an important point to remember. A FL in the past held that flag up and the break of the FL in the past creates a new FL holding price down. Bearing this in mind, the last blue box is our new FL, holding price up.

So, we've left our FLAG with an engulf, before carrying on towards the FL below (we're in a FL PAZ so we want the other side) but before we can carry on we need to go back to the source of our engulf, the RBD that caused the drop. After returning to our source we then engulf the previous low, creating the FL/FTR.

Jumping ahead, we engulf the upper limit of the red box, our FL FTR. It's no surprise we've looking for the same simple thing, we've engulfed so price wants to go back to the source of the move, the decision.

Why had price hit it's target? When we engulfed the engulf of our red FL we created a new FL. The decision to engulf and create this new FL and enter the PAZ above was the source of the move and was where the orders were as strong upward movement from the source shows.

There were other things to indicate we were going to return to this point. Price move in to CP above and then broke the source(FL) of the move in to the CP making our blue FL the target.

First of all my thought about FLs: they ARE a decision.

But not to Engulf. They are a decision that an EG is a real EG and not a FO! Therefore important.

Let's think about a rally: Price EG the last Supply level (SR or Supply) and searches for the next higher Balance (it is all a matter of Lots in both directions). In case of a FO, there is no Demand there anymore, so it still drops.

In case of Real EG the Buy orders take over again at a certain point, and the rally starts again - Taking over all the above Supply. That's the Battle Won! That's the DP and the FTR and the end (Limit) of the F.L.
